rationale.intuition:
Regression lock for PR #290: UMich publishes oosAcceptanceRate=18 while acceptanceRate=15.64 — an out-of-state rate slightly HIGHER than the overall (a known CDS data quirk). The pre-fix engine produced ratios > 1.3 which would have given an OOS applicant an absurd geographic *boost* at a flagship public. The fix clamps oos/overall to [0.35, 1.3] in geoMultiplier. For a strong OOS applicant at UMich the geo modifier caps at ≈1.15 (data-driven, ratio = 18/15.64), and the combined prediction must stay within the 8-30% reach band — never spike to the 35-50% match band that an unclamped ratio could produce.

If this fixture starts returning probabilities > 30%, suspect (a) the oos/overall clamp was relaxed, (b) the oosAcceptanceRate→ratio path was rewritten, or (c) the source data drifted.

sources.name: UMich CDS 2024-25 Section C
sources.evidence: Overall admit rate 15.64%; out-of-state Class of 2028 ~18% per Leland aggregator (seeded as oosAcceptanceRate=18). The 18 > 15.64 inversion is real CDS data, not a bug — but the engine must clamp the ratio.

sources.name: PR #290 — geoMultiplier ratio clamp
sources.evidence: Added Math.max(0.35, Math.min(1.3, oosRate / overallRate)) to bound geographic effect when oos data is counter-intuitive. Locked here to prevent silent regression.

sources.name: apps/api/scripts/closure-reports/overnight-2026-05-25/data-integrity-audit.md (Check 5a)
sources.evidence: Audit confirms 3 schools (SDSU, SUNY Binghamton, Cal Poly SLO) where oosAcceptanceRate > acceptanceRate + 30 — all flagship publics with self-selecting OOS pools. UMich is a milder case of the same pattern.

sources.name: Crimson Public Flagship OOS Benchmark 2024
sources.evidence: Strong OOS applicants at UMich (3.9/1480, no hooks) cluster at 10-25% per published case data — never 35%+.
